diff: This is supervised memory writing and reconstruction: the fully observed support legitimately includes the target payload. The student inference prompt contains only the question, without support, answer annotations, or retrieved text; the writer may read the complete observed note. Feature extraction disables the memory residual and freezes the backbone. S1 keys/values use the mean payload-span features; S3 uses each word-span mean. Spans are determined from observed text, not selected by the question or prediction. Address labels supervise offline training only and cannot enter queries or the VDB search API. S1 keys differ from the preceding last-token keys, so cross-round comparisons do not isolate data scale.

-To test composition rather than memorization of complete labels, each word position uses an explicit vocabulary with sufficient coverage in training A/B; the complete A/B triples belong to the training set. C/D are fixed draws of unseen complete combinations using trained words, avoiding unseen-token learning in this first stage. Report per-position word frequencies, complete-combination frequencies, token lengths, and first-token collisions in advance. C/D do not enter encoder centering, writer fitting, address training, optimizer updates, or checkpoint selection.

+To test composition rather than memorization of complete labels, each position uses an explicit 16-word vocabulary balanced in training A/B; the complete A/B triples belong to training. C/D retain the first two words of the corresponding A and replace only the third with another seen word, forming untrained complete triples. Their third words differ from each other and from that record in A/B. This specifically tests reading a new final word under an old prefix, not arbitrary-position or unseen-vocabulary generalization. Report per-position word frequencies, complete-combination frequencies, token lengths, and first-token collisions in advance. C/D do not enter encoder centering, writer fitting, address training, or optimizer updates; C is used only for endpoint development architecture selection, and D is never used for selection.

Training visits 16 targets in fixed shuffled epochs. Each update batches 16 sequences, with A samples before B samples; both worlds count toward balanced target exposure. Each sample has an independent bank. Its counterfactual bank starts from the common A bank and replaces only its own target, leaving other records in A. Do not switch all batch targets to B together or retrieve across samples. Bank rows have fixed data order; array positions are not query/writer input features, and target order is shuffled. Training steps, target schedules, and A/B ordering match across same-seed architecture arms. A/B views and repeated training do not increase the number of independent facts.
